title: The 10 Best Corded Rotary Hammers
subtitle: SDS-Plus rotary hammers for concrete and masonry, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A rotary hammer drills concrete, brick, and block much faster than a regular hammer drill, and most can switch to hammer-only mode for chipping tile or mortar. We ranked 10 corded SDS-Plus best-sellers on rating, review volume, and features (vibration control, a slip clutch, and bits and chisels in the box). They run from a $55 9-amp starter kit to $255 for the Makita HR2641.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

scoring.review_age_weighting: Listings under 24 months old with at least 30 reviews have their review count multiplied by min(2, 24 / age in months, age floored at 6) before scoring; older listings are unchanged. Listing age is Amazon's Date First Available, or an estimate from the ASIN when the listing does not show it.

avoid.name: VEVOR 1-1/4 Inch SDS-Plus Rotary Hammer Drill, 13 Amp Corded Drills, Heavy Duty Chipping Hammers w/Vibration Control & Safety Clutch
avoid.flag: Title says SDS-Plus and 13 A; bullets say SDS-Max, spec table 7 A
avoid.verdict: The listing can't agree on what this tool is. The title sells a 1-1/4 inch SDS-Plus hammer, the bullets describe an SDS-Max demolition hammer, and it costs about twice the ENEACRO 12.5 A, which publishes one consistent set of specs.
reasons: The title says SDS-Plus; the bullets say it has an SDS-Max chuck. The two take different bits, so you can't tell which bits to buy.
The title says 13 amps, the spec table says 7 amps, and the bullets claim 1,600 W and 25 J of impact, several times what any SDS-Plus hammer on this page is rated for.
The title says 1-1/4 inch, while the bullets and spec table give a 1-3/4 inch maximum drilling diameter.
At $209.25 it costs about $109 more than the ENEACRO 12.5 A, and the featured offer when we checked came from Amazon Resale rather than a new-stock seller.

buyers_guide.a: A hammer drill uses ridged clutch plates to rattle the bit. That's fine for a few 1/4" anchor holes in brick. A rotary hammer uses a piston to strike the bit, so it drills concrete several times faster, handles 1/2" and larger holes easily, and can chip in hammer-only mode. If you're drilling more than a handful of holes in concrete, get a rotary hammer.

buyers_guide.q: What is SDS-Plus, and do I need special bits?
buyers_guide.a: SDS-Plus is the shank and chuck system on every hammer on this page. The bit slides in and locks without a key, and it can slide back and forth so the piston can strike it. You need SDS-Plus bits and chisels. Regular round-shank bits won't fit without an adapter chuck, and SDS-Max bits are a larger, different size.

buyers_guide.q: How much impact energy do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Around 2 to 3 joules (1.5 to 2.2 ft-lb) handles anchor holes up to about 1/2" and light tile removal. The 13-amp hammers rated 5 to 7 joules are better for breaking floor tile, chiseling concrete, and holes over 3/4", but they weigh 12 lb or more. Brands don't all measure impact energy the same way, so treat small differences between brands with some skepticism.

buyers_guide.q: Is vibration control worth paying for?
buyers_guide.a: If you'll run it for more than a few minutes at a time, yes. Hammering vibration is what wears out your hands and arms. Makita's AVT counterweight cuts what reaches the handle; many budget tools only add a padded grip.

buyers_guide.q: Why don't the name-brand hammers include bits?
buyers_guide.a: The Makita HR2641 lists no bits in the box, so plan on buying them for the job. A decent SDS-Plus bit and chisel set runs $30 to $40. The budget brands bundle bits and chisels, which is handy for a first project, but those bits tend to wear out quickly.

buyers_guide.q: What does a safety clutch do?
buyers_guide.a: If the bit catches on rebar or jams in the hole, the motor's torque can twist the tool hard enough to hurt your wrist. A slip clutch or kickback sensor disconnects the drive when that happens. Every pick here lists one except the WORKPRO W125173A, whose listing doesn't mention it.
